requirements.requirement: node1 (OpenWrt dnsmasq) answers DNS for app.internal resolving to node2's IP (10.100.6.11) on the shared private network
requirements.summary: UCI dhcp.@domain entry added mapping app.internal -> 10.100.6.11, dnsmasq restarted, and nslookup against node1's LAN address (10.100.6.10) returns the correct answer both before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 exposes an HTTP service on TCP 8080 reachable over the shared network
requirements.summary: No listener on 8080 existed initially; executor created and enabled a systemd unit running python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080 and opened firewalld port 8080/tcp. IP-based reachability from node3 confirmed (HTTP 200), and the service returned to active/listening after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 reaches the service by the name app.internal via DNS resolution (through node1) with no local hosts-file entry
requirements.summary: node3's NetworkManager DNS was pointed at node1 (10.100.6.10) with auto-DNS ignored; getent hosts and curl confirm name resolution to 10.100.6.11 and HTTP 200, with /etc/hosts explicitly checked to contain no app.internal entry, both before and after node3's restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1, node2, node3 with pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a captured pre-restart boot_id, an issued reboot, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered functional state: node1's dnsmasq/DNS entry intact and resolving, node2's app8080 service returning to active/listening (after a ~70s network-online delay) with node3 confirming HTTP 200 by name, and node3's DNS config/resolution/HTTP reachability all confirmed post-reboot. The fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate all three boot_id transitions.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the core contract: node1's dnsmasq now authoritatively answers app.internal for the shared LAN, node2's previously-missing HTTP service on 8080 was stood up and made reachable, and node3 resolves and reaches the service purely via DNS with a verified absence of any /etc/hosts entry. The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot identity, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered DNS/HTTP functionality demonstrated after each reboot, directly corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: node2 shows a newly-failed NetworkManager-wait-online.service unit after its restart that was not present at baseline and was not investigated by the executor; it did not appear to block DNS/HTTP functionality but is an unresolved hygiene signal.

The task description implies node2's HTTP service pre-existed, but evidence shows it did not exist until the executor created it; this was a necessary and reasonable interpretation but is a deviation worth noting.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands chronologically. All mutations map to task outcomes or the mandated restart protocol: node2's app8080.service/firewalld port creation (required since the service was absent), node1's UCI dhcp domain entry and dnsmasq restart, node3's NetworkManager DNS reconfiguration, and the three native reboots. No abandoned troubleshooting mutations or unnecessary residue were found; temp-file diffs are ordinary reboot/session artifacts. One concern: after node2's restart, NetworkManager-wait-online.service is newly reported as failed (absent at before-prepare/baseline), which is a plausible side effect of the app8080.service unit's 'Wants=network-online.target' ordering interacting with boot timing; this residual failed-unit state was not investigated or remediated by the executor, though it did not prevent DNS/HTTP functionality from recovering.
